_status: NEW 2026-08-06. First New Zealand nodes in the corpus, and the second country in the `SAO` ('South Asia + Oceania') colour family after Australia (src/lib/palette.ts). Depth pass on central -> local government finance, on the same model as the Netherlands, UK and Australia passes. Same working session as `AU/G.1.md`; Thomas asked for New Zealand directly after Australia.
_note:
Three general-purpose subagents researched this in parallel (central->local funding: NZTA Funding Assistance Rates, LGA 2002, LGFA, central grant methodologies / the rating-valuation chain / accounting standards + statistics). EVERY quote below was then independently re-fetched and re-verified by this session's own tooling before minting: xrb.govt.nz, treasury.govt.nz, datainfoplus.stats.govt.nz, wellington.govt.nz, lgfa.co.nz and linz.govt.nz all served raw bytes to plain curl (HTML tag-stripped, or pypdf-extracted for PDFs). legislation.govt.nz is behind an AWS WAF that returns HTTP 202 with zero bytes to every non-browser client tried, so the two Acts were read from the Parliamentary Counsel Office's own PDFs replayed byte-for-byte through the Wayback `id_` endpoint (Local Government (Rating) Act 2002, version as at 27 November 2025; Rating Valuations Act 1998, version as at 23 December 2023), and the Local Government Act 2002 from a FAOLEX mirror of the PCO reprint as at 26 March 2020 -- flagged per-edge where the version matters. nzta.govt.nz and mbie.govt.nz returned HTTP 403 to direct curl and were likewise read via Wayback `id_` raw replay of the official pages. No AI-summarising fetch tool produced any quote in this file.

ADDENDUM 2026-08-06 (second thread, browser session). The `legislation.govt.nz` blocker described above is RESOLVED and the slice's load-bearing statutory chain has been re-read first-hand from the current consolidation, replacing the Wayback and FAOLEX proxy reads. The site renders normally in a browser; note for successors that its article-text extractor returns nothing, so the working route is DOM extraction against `div.prov`, and a session that only tries a text extractor will wrongly conclude the domain is dead. The chain, verified link by link and quoted verbatim: LGA 2002 s 111(1) "All information that is required by any provision of this Part or of Schedule 10 to be included in any plan, report, or other document must be prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting practice if that information is of a form or nature for which generally accepted accounting practice has developed standards." -> LGA 2002 s 5(1) "generally accepted accounting practice has the same meaning as in section 8 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013" -> FRA 2013 s 8 "In this Act, financial statements, group financial statements, a report, or other information complies with generally accepted accounting practice only if the report, statements, or information comply with— (a) applicable financial reporting standards; and (b) in relation to matters for which no provision is made in applicable financial reporting standards, an authoritative notice." -> FRA 2013 s 5(1) "financial reporting standard means a financial reporting standard issued by the Board under section 12" and "Board means the External Reporting Board continued under section 11". The chain therefore terminates in the XRB by statutory definition, as `G.1.md` claimed, and the claim no longer rests on a proxy read of any kind. IMPORTANT VERSION POINT: the earlier LGA 2002 read was of a reprint as at 26 March 2020; this read is of the current consolidation, and s 111(2) ("Subsection (1) does not apply to the preparation of a funding impact statement", added 27 November 2010) is present and unchanged. Cheap check 5 of `NZ/G.3.md` is closed. What remains unverified is the exhaustive Schedule 10 sweep, which is still a subagent's grep — see the `_dropped` entry for it.

reports.title: Financial Statements of the Government of New Zealand
reports.description: The audited annual financial statements of the whole New Zealand government reporting entity, presented to Parliament as paper B.11. New Zealand's analog of Canada's Public Accounts. Prepared under the Public Finance Act 1989 and NZ GAAP as defined in the Financial Reporting Act 2013, on Public Sector PBE Accounting Standards Tier 1. The Treasury also publishes interim (monthly, year-to-date) financial statements through the year; `releases_per_year` counts the audited year-end set only.
reports.cadence_note: One audited year-end set (B.11), plus roughly eleven interim monthly year-to-date sets on the same basis; `releases_per_year` counts the audited set only, since the interim statements are the same document unaudited rather than a separate release.

reports.title: Budget Economic and Fiscal Update
reports.description: The Treasury's Budget-day economic and fiscal forecasts, parliamentary paper B.3, required by the Public Finance Act 1989. Its forecasts become the 'Budget 20XX' comparatives in the following year's Financial Statements of the Government. A Half Year Economic and Fiscal Update (HYEFU) on the same statutory footing appears each December, and a Pre-election Update in election years; `releases_per_year` counts BEFU alone.
reports.cadence_note: BEFU annually in May; the companion HYEFU each December makes two statutory Updates a year, three in election years.

reports.title: Government finance statistics (general government)
reports.description: Stats NZ's annual consolidation of central and local government financial activity on the IMF's GFS framework — the direct counterpart of Australia's `au-abs-gfs`. Its own DataInfo+ metadata sets out a two-source split that is unusually explicit for this corpus: central government from the Treasury's CFISnet database, local government from the annual Local Authority Census supplemented by individual councils' annual reports.

reports.title: Local authority statistics (quarterly)
reports.description: Quarterly income and expenditure statistics for New Zealand's 11 regional councils and 68 territorial authorities, collected through the Quarterly Local Authority Survey (QLAS, questionnaire BS/QS/01). Provisional until benchmarked against the annual Local Authority Census, and fed forward into the national accounts and into Government finance statistics as the provisional local-government estimate.

reports.title: Local Authority Census / Local Authority Financial Statistics
reports.description: The annual census of all city, district and regional councils and their non-market council-controlled organisations, and the Local Authority Financial Statistics (LAFS) compiled from it — the more comprehensive, less timely annual counterpart to QLAS. Stats NZ's own metadata states that LAFS is 'no longer published in the information release format used for 2009-13' and directs users to Infoshare instead, so the release exists as a data update rather than as a titled information release; kept as one node for that reason.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, released around May for the June year ending 11 months earlier. Distributed via Infoshare rather than as a titled information release since the 2009-13 series ended.

reports.title: National accounts (income, saving, assets, and liabilities)
reports.description: Stats NZ's quarterly institutional-sector accounts, including the net operating surplus series that the Treasury uses to uplift company tax estimates in the Financial Statements of the Government. Named in FSGNZ 2025 by its exact release URL rather than by title — the most specific Treasury-to-Stats-NZ citation found this session.

reports.title: Local authority annual reports
reports.description: The audited annual report every local authority must adopt under Local Government Act 2002 s.98, containing the information required by Part 3 of Schedule 10 (including, per clause 29, audited financial statements, and per clause 30A the district's rating-unit count and total capital and land values). Held as a class node — the exact counterpart of Australia's `au-la-annual-statements` — because Stats NZ, the LGFA and MBIE all name the class rather than any one council's report. `nz-wellington-annual-report` is this slice's specific exemplar.
reports.cadence_note: One per local authority per financial year, adopted within four months of 30 June (LGA 2002 s.98(3)).

reports.title: Wellington City Council Annual Report (Te Pūrongo ā-Tau)
reports.description: This slice's exemplar council annual report, Volume 2 (Financial Statements) of the 2024/25 report. Chosen over Auckland and Christchurch on availability grounds: Auckland Council's site returns HTTP 406 and Christchurch's HTTP 403 to every non-browser client tried, while wellington.govt.nz serves the PDF to plain curl. Its Statement of Compliance and its Note 1 together close the New Zealand accounting-standard chain from the council's own side — see the `nz-pbe-ipsas-1` edge, and contrast Brisbane's refusal to name AASB 1049 in `au-government-finance.json`.

reports.title: Wellington City Council rating valuations and rates
reports.description: Wellington City Council's own published account of how its rates are struck on rating values — the New Zealand counterpart to `au-georges-river-rates`. States that values are determined by Quotable Value on a three-yearly cycle, that the process is governed by the Rating Valuations Act 1998 and audited by the Office of the Valuer-General, and that the council sends building-consent details to QV between revaluations. NOTE: the page writes 'Rating Valuation Act 1998', dropping the 's' from the Act's actual short title 'Rating Valuations Act 1998' — quoted verbatim in the edge basis rather than silently corrected.
reports.cadence_note: Rates are set annually; the underlying rating valuation behind them is revised three-yearly (latest effective 1 September 2024, next 2027).

reports.title: District valuation roll (general revaluation)
reports.publisher: New Zealand territorial authorities; certified by the Valuer-General
reports.description: The roll of every rating unit in a territorial authority's district, prepared and maintained under Rating Valuations Act 1998 s.7 and revalued in full at intervals of not more than three years under s.9. The rating equivalent of the Netherlands' WOZ beschikking and NSW's Valuer-General land values. Its statutory gate is unusually hard: s.11(2) forbids assessing any rate on the proposed values until the Valuer-General has certified approval of the general revaluation.
reports.cadence_note: Three-yearly per territorial authority (RVA 1998 s.9(1)), staggered across the 66 territorial authorities, so several fall due nationally each year.

reports.title: Rating Valuations Act 1998
reports.publisher: Parliamentary Counsel Office (administered by Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand)
reports.description: The Act creating the Valuer-General (s.3), setting the Valuer-General's standard-setting, monitoring and certification functions (s.4), empowering the Rating Valuations Rules (s.5), requiring each territorial authority to keep a district valuation roll (s.7), requiring three-yearly general revaluation (s.9) and forbidding rates to be assessed on uncertified values (s.11(2)). Structural counterpart of New South Wales' `au-vola1916`, minted on the same convention that a periodically reprinted statute is a node when downstream documents cite it by name.
reports.cadence_note: A consolidated statute, reprinted on amendment rather than published on a schedule; version read this session is 'as at 23 December 2023'.

reports.title: Rating Valuations Rules 2008 (LINZS30300)
reports.publisher: Office of the Valuer-General, Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand
reports.description: The Valuer-General's secondary legislation prescribing what the district valuation roll must contain, how sale details must be captured and coded, and the statistical rules a proposed revaluation must satisfy against market sales evidence (rule 5.5.1: coefficient of dispersion ≤ 12, median value price ratio 0.9–1.1, price related differential 0.98–1.03). Version date 1 October 2010; LINZ's own review page (fetched 2026-08) says replacement rules were expected to go to formal consultation in 2026, so this node's edition is likely to move.
reports.cadence_note: Amended rarely — Version 3.0 (2002), 3.1 (2003), 2008 issue, 31 March 2009 issue, 1 October 2010 issue. A review was under way as at July 2025.

reports.title: XRB A1 Application of the Accounting Standards Framework
reports.description: The XRB standard that allocates every reporting entity to a tier and to a for-profit / public-benefit-entity track, and defines 'public sector PBE' by cross-reference to the Public Audit Act 2001. THE FINDING OF THIS SLICE LIVES HERE: XRB A1 never uses the words 'local authority' or 'Local Government Act' anywhere in its 43 pages (grep of the full extracted text, 0 hits) — like Australia's AASB 1049 and unlike the Netherlands' BBV or the UK's CIPFA Code, the standard does not name local government in its own scope.
reports.cadence_note: Issued 10 December 2015; compiled version read this session 'incorporates amendments to 31 March 2024'.

reports.title: PBE IPSAS 1 Presentation of Financial Reports
reports.publisher: New Zealand Accounting Standards Board / External Reporting Board (XRB)
reports.description: The presentation standard for Tier 1 and Tier 2 public benefit entities, which is what New Zealand councils report under. Like XRB A1, it names no local authority: grep of its full 54 pages returns 0 hits for 'local authority', 'Local Government Act' and 'Public Audit Act'. The only local-government hook in its text is the word 'ratepayers' in the list of users of general purpose financial reports (para 3), which is not a scope binding. The binding is achieved instead by a statutory chain outside the standard — see the `nz-wellington-annual-report` edge.
reports.cadence_note: Issued September 2014; version read this session incorporates amendments to 31 January 2022 with further amendments effective 1 January 2026.

reports.title: LGFA Annual Report
reports.publisher: New Zealand Local Government Funding Agency (LGFA)
reports.description: The annual report of the joint council-and-Crown-owned agency that raises debt on behalf of New Zealand councils — an institution with no direct Australian, Dutch or UK counterpart in this corpus. Names councils' own statutory planning documents as the material it monitors against its lending covenants. NEGATIVE FINDING recorded here: grep of the full 77-page 2025 report returns 0 hits for 'Statistics New Zealand', 'Stats NZ' and 'census' — LGFA's covenants are defined on accounting aggregates, not on any named statistical release.

reports.title: Funding Assistance Rates (FAR) Policy
reports.description: The policy that sets, once per three-year National Land Transport Programme, the share of each council's land transport programme the National Land Transport Fund co-invests. New Zealand's closest structural analog to the funding-formula technical annexes that anchored the Netherlands, UK, Ontario and Tasmania slices — and it is DELIBERATELY ISOLATED in this graph, because it names none of its four inputs to a titled source. See this slice's `_dropped` array for the verbatim negative. The isolation is the finding, on the convention `EU/G.47.md` established for `nordic-statistics-database` and `AU/G.1.md` reused for `au-brisbane-financial-statements`.
reports.cadence_note: Normal FARs are recalculated once per three-year NLTP cycle; the policy page itself is a living document (issued February 2021, last updated August 2023).

reports.title: Tourism Infrastructure Fund: application and assessment process
reports.description: MBIE's published assessment process for the Tourism Infrastructure Fund, which allocates central-government co-funding to councils for visitor-related infrastructure. The only New Zealand central-government allocation document found this session that names its own territorial-authority-level data inputs by exact title. CADENCE CAVEAT: TIF ran in numbered rounds (Round 7 opened April 2023) rather than on a fixed schedule, and the round cadence is the weakest part of this node's claim to be a recurrent release.
reports.cadence_note: Round-based rather than periodic — roughly annual rounds, with the assessment page revised per round.

reports.title: Accommodation Data Programme
reports.description: MBIE's monthly commercial-accommodation guest-night series, collected from accommodation providers and reported at territorial-authority level. Successor to the Stats NZ Accommodation Survey. Named by exact title in the Tourism Infrastructure Fund's assessment process as the source of the guest-night half of its eligibility ratio.

reports.title: Tourism Electronic Card Transactions (TECTs)
reports.description: MBIE's monthly estimates of tourism spending derived from electronic card transaction data, published by territorial authority and region. Named by exact title and acronym in the Tourism Infrastructure Fund's assessment process as the source of the regional tourism-revenue eligibility test.

reports.title: Annual Report of the Controller and Auditor-General
reports.publisher: Controller and Auditor-General of New Zealand (Office of the Auditor-General / The Audit Office)
reports.description: The Auditor-General's statutory annual report to the House of Representatives, required by section 37 of the Public Audit Act 2001. Minted 2026-08-06 to close the branch's highest-value single gap: the corpus held no node for the New Zealand Auditor-General's own recurring output, which is what blocked the Tokelau half of the export-of-institution finding. The report is where the office states, in its own words and every year, the extent of its mandate, including the two jurisdictions outside New Zealand it serves.
reports.cadence_note: Annual and statutory. Public Audit Act 2001 s 37(1): "As soon as practicable after the end of each financial year, the Auditor-General must prepare and present an annual report to the House of Representatives in accordance with section 43 of the Public Finance Act 1989." s 37(2) requires it to include "an account of the implementation of the annual plan required under section 36" and "a list of entities audited by the Auditor-General under an arrangement in accordance with section 19". The 2024/25 edition is 108 pages.

reports.title: Public Audit Act 2001
reports.publisher: Parliamentary Counsel Office (administered by the Office of the Auditor-General)
reports.description: The statute that constitutes the Auditor-General, defines 'public entity', and requires the annual plan (s 36) and the annual report (s 37). Minted 2026-08-06 because it was already load-bearing in this corpus without a node: XRB A1 defines 'public sector PBE' by cross-reference to it, Wellington City Council self-classifies under it, and the Tokelau audit mandate turns on it. Schedule 2, 'Specific public entities not falling within any class' (s 5(1)(d)), lists "Tokelau Administration" by name. A full-text search of the current consolidation returns one occurrence of 'Tokelau' and zero of 'Niue' — which is the sharpest single piece of evidence for the export-of-institution finding, because it shows New Zealand statute reaching into Tokelau and being silent on Niue, whose Constitution instead reaches out.
reports.cadence_note: A consolidated statute, reprinted on amendment rather than published on a schedule. Version read 2026-08-06 is the current consolidation on legislation.govt.nz, which carries amendments through the Taranaki Maunga Collective Redress Act 2025 in Schedule 2.

"To provide fair, transparent property rates, we use standard rating valuations governed by the Rating Valuation Act 1998 and audited by the Office of the Valuer-General." VERIFIED DIRECTLY (Local Government (Rating) Act 2002, version as at 27 November 2025, read from the Parliamentary Counsel Office's own PDF replayed byte-for-byte through the Wayback `id_` endpoint because legislation.govt.nz's WAF returns HTTP 202 with zero bytes to non-browser clients; pypdf-extracted, 129 pages). The chain is entirely in statute, in four hops. s.13(3): "For the purposes of this section, the rateable value of the land— (a) must be— (i) the annual value of the land; or (ii) the capital value of the land; or (iii) the land value of the land; and (b) must be identified in the local authority's funding impact statement as the value for setting a general rate." s.5 pins each of those three to the other Act: "capital value has the meaning set out in section 2(1) of the Rating Valuations Act 1998" (identically for annual value and land value). s.27(4): "The database must include, in relation to each rating unit within the local authority's district,— (a) all information that relates to the unit that is included in the district valuation roll for the district". s.5 again: "district valuation roll means,— (a) in relation to a territorial authority, a roll prepared for a district under section 7 of the Rating Valuations Act 1998 and approved under section 11 of that Act". This is New Zealand's exact counterpart to NSW Local Government Act 1993 s.498's cross-Act citation of the Valuation of Land Act 1916.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY (Rating Valuations Act 1998, version as at 23 December 2023, PCO PDF via Wayback `id_` raw replay, pypdf-extracted, 43 pages). s.7(1): "Each territorial authority must prepare and maintain a district valuation roll for its own district in accordance with rules made under this Act." s.9(1): "A territorial authority must revise its district valuation roll at intervals of not more than 3 years by revaluing every rating unit within its district to ensure that the roll represents values current as at the date of the revaluation." s.11(2), the hard gate: "No rate may be assessed on the basis of the values proposed in the general revaluation unless the Valuer-General has certified his or her approval of the general revaluation under this section." s.4(1)(b) gives the Valuer-General the function "to set minimum quality standards and specifications necessary for the maintenance and upkeep of district valuation rolls..."

VERIFIED DIRECTLY (both documents read this session — RVA 1998 as above; Rating Valuations Rules 2008 LINZS30300 version date 1 October 2010, the official linz.govt.nz PDF replayed through Wayback `id_`, pypdf-extracted, 79 pages). RVA s.7(1) requires the roll to be maintained "in accordance with rules made under this Act" and s.7(2) that "Each roll must contain the information in respect of each rating unit within the district that is required by the rules"; s.9(3) requires each general revaluation to "comply with rules made by the Valuer-General for the purpose". The Rules then set the content (rule 2.1), the sale-detail capture (rule 4.4.2: "The territorial authority must enter sale details in the DVR supporting information, as set out in rule 2.2, within 15 working days of receiving the necessary documentation") and the acceptance test (rule 5.5.1: "Where capital values or only land values are assessed, the proposed values, when compared to the market sales evidence, must satisfy the following statistical rules where appropriate: (a) coefficient of dispersion, which must be equal to or less than 12, (b) median value price ratio, which must be within the range 0.9 to 1.1, (c) price related differential which must be within the range 0.98 and 1.03, and (d) comparison of average value changes between sold and unsold properties, which must be equal to or less than 5 %.").

The appendix then enumerates the departures, which confirms this is adoption-with-amendment rather than a passing reference: "The significant differences between PBE IPSAS 1 and IPSAS 1 are: (a) The title of PBE IPSAS 1 reflects the fact that it establishes presentation requirements for both financial statements and service performance information. VERIFIED DIRECTLY by this session (2026-08-06, second thread): the Act read in a browser on legislation.govt.nz, the annual report's own text extracted from the 108-page PDF at ao.parliament.nz. The report states its governing instruments in its own front matter: "The annual report informs our stakeholders – Parliament, New Zealanders, and public organisations – about our strategic intentions, priorities, and performance for the year 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025. It has been prepared in keeping with the requirements of the Public Audit Act 2001 and the Public Finance Act 1989, as well as recent guidance provided by the Treasury." The Act supplies both the obligation and the required contents — s 37(1): "As soon as practicable after the end of each financial year, the Auditor-General must prepare and present an annual report to the House of Representatives in accordance with section 43 of the Public Finance Act 1989." s 37(2): "The report must include— ... (b) an account of the implementation of the annual plan required under section 36; and (c) a list of entities audited by the Auditor-General under an arrangement in accordance with section 19." This is methodology_depends_on rather than cites because the statute dictates the report's contents, not merely its existence. NOTE the Public Finance Act 1989 is named in the same sentence and is not a node; recorded as a lead in `_dropped`.

_dropped.why: VERIFIED DIRECTLY (the official NZTA page replayed through Wayback `id_` raw bytes after nzta.govt.nz returned HTTP 403 to direct curl). This is the New Zealand equivalent of the document that carried the Netherlands, UK, Ontario and Tasmania slices — a national formula deciding how much central money each council gets — and it names none of its inputs to a titled release. Verbatim, the whole of its "Inputs" section: "Inputs for each approved organisation are: centreline kilometres, which provide a measure of the length of the road network to be maintained and services to be available to all transport users / capital value, which is used by most local authorities to set rates, and provides a measure of the asset base from which local authorities raise their local share / inverse of rating units, which identifies local authorities that have the smallest number of ratepayers from which to source their local share / index of deprivation, a demographic index published by the University of Otago and used by the Ministry of Health, which provides a measure of the relative wealth of communities / total cost of all activities for a recent period, which is the actual total costs incurred by approved organisations for the last 3 to 5 years." And "Setting normal FARs": "A year before the start of each NLTP, we recalculate the normal FAR for each approved organisation by inputting the latest available information. The changes in FARs, if any, will reflect movements in centreline kilometres, capital values, rating units and the index of deprivation." Two publishers are named for the deprivation index and no title; the other three inputs are sourced anonymously, even though 'capital value' and 'rating units' are exactly the figures LGA 2002 Schedule 10 clause 30A makes councils publish. `nz-nzta-far-policy` is therefore minted and left isolated, on the `au-brisbane-financial-statements` convention — the absence is the result.

_dropped.edge: council long-term plan / development contributions policy -> Producers Price Index Outputs for Construction
_dropped.why: VERIFIED DIRECTLY (Local Government Act 2002, PCO reprint as at 26 March 2020, read from a FAOLEX mirror PDF because legislation.govt.nz's WAF blocks non-browser clients; pypdf-extracted, 469 pages). s.106(2C): "A development contribution may be increased under subsection (2B) only if— (a) the increase does not exceed the result of multiplying together— (i) the rate of increase (if any), in the Producers Price Index Outputs for Construction provided by Statistics New Zealand since the development contribution was last set or increased..." This is the ONLY place in the whole Act where a Stats NZ release is named by title rather than by agency, and it is a real formula link. Not minted because neither endpoint is a node yet: the citing side is a council's development contributions policy (part of the long-term plan), and the cited side is a series inside the Producers Price Index rather than a standalone release. Note also a title-drift problem for whoever builds it — the modern Stats NZ product is 'Producers price index' with a construction-industry outputs series, not a release called 'Producers Price Index Outputs for Construction'. VERSION CAVEAT: the reprint read is five years old; re-check s.106(2C) against the current consolidation before building.

_dropped.edge: Rating Valuations Rules 2008 -> a titled land-registry sales dataset
_dropped.why: VERIFIED DIRECTLY (full 79-page LINZS30300 text grepped case-insensitively). New Zealand has NO counterpart to the NSW chain's "NSW property sales information comes from Notices of Sale lodged with Land Registry Services" or to the Netherlands' Waarderingsinstructie naming Kadaster. Hits: 'Landonline' 0, 'notice of sale' 0, 'Registrar-General' 0, 'tax statement' 0, 'Quotable' 0. The Rules require sale details to be captured and coded (rules 2.2, 4.4.2, Appendix G) and the Valuer-General to analyse "All market sales and market rentals for whole rating units that are relevant to the effective date of the revaluation" (rule 5.5 commentary) — but they name a data CATEGORY and never a register, form or titled release. Building consents are likewise named as a category held by the territorial authority itself (rules 4.7.6, 4.7.7), corroborated from the council side by Wellington City Council's "Between three-yearly revaluations, we send details of all building consents to Quotable Value". This is a genuine structural difference from both the Australian and Dutch chains, not a search failure.

_dropped.edge: LINZ property transfers and tax residency data -> the rating valuation chain
_dropped.why: VERIFIED DIRECTLY (linz.govt.nz page fetched with plain curl). The obvious candidate for the missing sales-evidence source is LINZ's transfer tax statement data, whose quarterly reports Stats NZ took over in 2018. LINZ's own page rules it out: "Information on the size or value of the property being transferred is not included in this report as this is not collected in the tax statements." No value and no size means it cannot be the input to a mass-appraisal revaluation. Recorded so a future session does not spend the same hour rediscovering it.

_dropped.edge: XRB A1 / PBE IPSAS 1 -> local authorities, by name
_dropped.why: VERIFIED DIRECTLY (both standards downloaded from xrb.govt.nz with plain curl and pypdf-extracted in full, then grepped). XRB A1, 43 pages: 'local authorit' 0 hits, 'Local Government Act' 0 hits. PBE IPSAS 1, 54 pages: 'local authorit' 0, 'Local Government Act' 0, 'Public Audit Act' 0. The only local-government word anywhere in PBE IPSAS 1 is 'ratepayers', in para 3's list of users of general purpose financial reports — not a scope clause. New Zealand's accounting standards bind councils the way Australia's AASB 1049 does not and the Netherlands' BBV and the UK's CIPFA Code do: NOT by naming them. What differs from Australia is that the binding still happens, transitively and entirely in statute — LGA 2002 s.111 ("All information that is required by any provision of this Part or of Schedule 10 to be included in any plan, report, or other document must be prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting practice...") → LGA 2002 s.5 ("generally accepted accounting practice has the same meaning as in section 8 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013") → Financial Reporting Act 2013 s.8 → XRB standards; and the Financial Reporting Act's own definition of 'entity' expressly includes "a local authority (within the meaning of section 5(1) of the Local Government Act 2002)". The LGA quotes are VERIFIED DIRECTLY from the FAOLEX mirror of the PCO reprint as at 26 March 2020; the Financial Reporting Act 2013 text was NOT independently re-verified this session (legislation.govt.nz blocked; a subagent read it through a text-extraction proxy) and should be re-read before being relied on. The one XRB-published document that does name local government is the XRB website's own Accounting Standards Framework page — "Local bodies and council controlled organisations (CCOs) under the Local Government Act 2002" — VERIFIED DIRECTLY, but a web page rather than a standard, so it carries no edge.

_dropped.edge: nz-lgfa-annual-report -> council long-term plans and annual plans
_dropped.why: The same LGFA sentence that carries the minted annual-reports edge also names "annual plans and long-term plans" — the LGA 2002 s.95 and s.93 documents. Neither is a node yet. The long-term plan in particular is the richest unbuilt New Zealand node available: three-yearly, statutorily required to contain a financial strategy (s.101A), an infrastructure strategy (s.101B) and a funding impact statement, and separately audited by the Auditor-General, who publishes an observations report per cycle. Deliberately left for a second New Zealand session rather than half-built here.

_dropped.edge: Local Government Act 2002 Schedule 10 -> any named statistical or accounting publication
_dropped.why: NOT INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED as an exhaustive sweep — a subagent extracted the full Schedule 10 (Parts 1-4, clauses 1-37) and grepped it, reporting zero occurrences of any Stats NZ release, Valuer-General document, LINZ product or accounting standard, with every external reference being to another Act. NOT MINTED, against the recommendation of `NZ/G.2.md` item 1, which listed this as one of three 'free' edges. The single sentence offered as its basis is: "In 2018, we implemented the Government Finance Statistics Manual 2014 (GFSM2014), which follows the GFSM 2001 and is consistent with the System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA08)." Read carefully, the subject of 'is consistent with the System of National Accounts 2008' is GFSM2014, not Stats NZ's release: the sentence documents a relation between two international manuals and Stats NZ's adoption of one of them. It does not state that the New Zealand GFS release takes SNA 2008 as an input, and 'is consistent with' is in any case a weaker claim than any of the four `relationship_type` values, all of which describe an input. Compare the four edges the corpus already holds into `sna-2008` — `ck-national-accounts` ("The conceptual framework used to compile the Cook Islands GDP is based on the System of National Accounts 2008"), `statcan-national-accounts`, `bea-gdp` and `fed-z1` — every one of which is a first-person statement by the producer about its own product. Grep of every New Zealand source cached by the minting session returns SNA 2008 in this one sentence only. The honest edge available from this sentence is `imf-gfsm -> sna-2008`, a framework-to-framework link the corpus has no precedent for and which should be sourced to the IMF's own manual rather than to a third country's metadata page; left for a session that can read GFSM 2014 directly. If Stats NZ's national accounts releases are ever scouted, `nz-statsnz-national-accounts-income -> sna-2008` is the likely real edge.

That is a documented dependency of the council's annual report on the Act, and the only reason it is not minted here is that the quote is a predecessor's extraction rather than this session's read, and this session held itself to first-hand reads. Re-fetch Wellington Volume 2 and mint it; it is one lookup. The PFA is not a node and is a larger question than this slice, because it would sit under a great many New Zealand fiscal releases at once — deferred deliberately, and it is probably the right next statute to mint.
